quest.title: The Raven's Legacy
quest.description: The Great Treasure is within reach...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

chapter.title: East of the Moon, West of the Sun

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tolfin! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Ah, fantastic, just the duo I was waiting for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How did you know we would come here? H—Have you been following us since we parted at Blue Amber Lake!?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Haha! I was only joking. I came back to visit my parents and just so happened to be running errands here in Piramida when I spotted the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sees... Huh? So you have family here?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: What's strange about that? Just like a raven is born to raven parents, people don't magically appear out of thin air.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not what Paimon meant! Hmm... Though come to think of it, we're not really that close, and Paimon can see how it was kind of a personal question...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can I ask a question that isn't so personal?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good idea! Tolfin knows everyone and everything — he just might have the info we need.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount your experiences searching for, and finding, the Proofs of the Cognoscenti after leaving Blue Amber Lake...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Tolfin, do you have any idea where the last Proof of the Cognoscenti might be?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: I do have a few thoughts, however...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: #Hmm, seeing as it's {NICKNAME}, {M#he}{F#she}'ll probably be fine. From everything I've heard about your adventures, I believe {M#he}{F#she} should be able to overcome the trial.

choices.text: There's another trial? ...It isn't going to be impossible, is it?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #Of course not. Besides, I have total confidence in your abilities, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Ahem, the last Proof of the Cognoscenti is actually with my grandmother. I'm on my way to visit her now — why don't you tag along?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Seriously?! What are the chances? Tolfin's grandmother... What do you think she's like, {NICKNAME}? Do you think she's the kind of sweet old lady who loves to tell stories?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: She does tell stories, but... Never mind, you'll see when we get there.

choices.text: Then why didn't you tell us about it back at Blue Amber Lake...?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Mmm... Well, the fact we can meet here again is a sign that our fates are somehow intertwined. Rather than dwell on the past, we should look toward the future instead...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow. That change of subject couldn't have felt any more forced if you'd tried!

talks.objective: Go to Piramida to look for clues
Go to the place indicated by Tolfin

dialogues.text: Well, well, well, look who's remembered to visit! Did you take care of that matter for me, you little brat?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Of course I did! Would I dare show my face here if I hadn't?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Ahem... This is my grandmother. Though I'm sure she'd rather be known as "Hiljetta, the Black-Barrel Hag" than "a failed merchant's grandmother."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She doesn't look anything like Tolfin at all... She's far too serious...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I hear that a lot. But at the end of the day, we're family, and we're a lot more alike than people think.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #This is {NICKNAME}, and this is Paimon. They've already found the other Proofs of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: Oh? So you've already found the other four? Well, that takes some real talent. But I'm afraid you're going to have to let me see that talent for myself.

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: Seeing as the brat brought you in, I won't make things too hard for you — how about we just trade a few moves?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on a second! This... uhm... Something about this doesn't feel right...

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: And what exactly is the problem? If you want to get your hands on the Great Treasure, you'll naturally need to get past me first.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #She's a stubborn old bag of bones, but once she sees what you can do, everything'll be on the table. Come on, {NICKNAME}, it's in your hands now.

choices.text: You don't look much like Tolfin.

talks.objective: Have a friendly spar with the Black-Barrel Hag

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, it mentions Brahe over here. Looks like he was the one who made these records.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Iron Coins were really the currency here back in the day... That means a mountain of these things could truly be called a "Great Treasure."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, if only we'd come here a few hundred years ago, we'd be rich! But Iron Coins aren't worth much Mora these days...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: As they say, value lies in scarcity...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly. So if we can find this... Prototype Iron Coin he wrote about, collectors are sure to go crazy for it! Paimon bets we could get a pretty penny for that one!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Too bad we don't know where it's buried. Ugh... Are we really supposed to dig up this whole place by ourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll get a dressing down from the Black-Barrel Hag if we don't.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah... you're right. We mustn't get on the wrong side of her. You might be able to handle her attacks, but Paimon will have to fly far, far away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And speaking of the Black-Barrel Hag... now that Paimon has seen Brahe's notes and all these Iron Coins, she finally understands why that old lady wants to bring back the good old days.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: To her, those days must have been the real Elysium.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks we're living in a pretty wonderful time, too! You and Paimon, and all the friends we've met on our journey... This is our golden age!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's probably how Tolfin feels as well. He chose not to share the full history of the Treasure Hoarders with us because he didn't want us to bear the weight of expectation...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* It looks like this adventure ends here. Getting all five Proofs of the Cognoscenti wasn't easy, and Paimon knows it was far from a fruitless journey, but she can't help feeling a little disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way... Why do you think this ship is here?

choices.text: Perhaps it sank under the weight of a greed it could not bear...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It would be risky to sail with all those heavy coins on board... Even if they didn't sink, they might get robbed! Oh, but this is a Treasure Hoarder ship — they're not usually the ones who would need to be scared.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's such a shame. Even though this ship is hundreds of years old, it still looks almost new. Traveling would be so much easier if we had a boat as big as this, don't you think?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll be the captain, and Paimon, you can be the chief mate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Aye aye, Cap'n {NICKNAME}! Tying the jib to the mizzenmast and raising the port side anchor to the load line, Cap'n!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, how convincing is Paimon's chief mateyness? Come on, take the helm, and let's set sail!

choices.text: Maybe it's a ship of dreams that ran aground before it ever set sail...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That must mean this is the Treasure Hoarders' secret dock! Hundreds of years have passed now, and the local geography's changed — Paimon figures it's probably never going to get the chance...

talks.objective: Talk to Hiljetta

dialogues.speaker: Hiljetta
dialogues.text: Not bad, not bad at all! You do have promise. Here, this is the Proof of the Cognoscenti you've been seeking. But if you want to claim the Great Treasure, there's still one final path you'll have to tread.

dialogues.speaker: Hiljetta
dialogues.text: #Not that it'll hold {M#him}{F#her} back — not considering how sharp the little {M#lad}{F#lass} is. {M#He}{F#She}'s a far more fitting heir to the Treasure Hoarders than you are, ya useless lump.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Heir to the Treasure Hoarders? Me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So Granny is a Treasure Hoarder? And Tolfin, you too?

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: I guess you could say that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon never would've guessed. You don't look like a Treasure Hoarder. Don't tell Paimon you knew about this all along, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I figured it out pretty quickly...

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: ...Don't tell me you didn't explain it to them? Were you really planning to deliver the Great Treasure to a couple of know-nothings who couldn't tell a Treasure Hoarder if they introduced themselves and brought them to their grandmother?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: They've shown they have what it takes to gather the Proofs of the Cognoscenti — and they handled your challenge just fine. In fact, weren't you praising them just now?

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: You little...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #Alright, alright, don't give yourself a heart attack... I'll explain everything to them right now. I'll see to it that {NICKNAME} is willing to be the Treasure Hoarders' heir — exactly as you wanted!

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: Hmph! And you really think you can make all of that clear to them lickety-split?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: What are you so worried about? You won't shut up about how I'm just like that "good-for-nothing Brahe." At least I inherited his gift for smooth talking, didn't I?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tolfin leads you to a quiet corner to talk...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what's really going on here? All we heard is that if we collect all five Proofs of the Cognoscenti, we can find the Great Treasure hidden "East of the Moon, West of the Sun"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you seriously telling Paimon that we'd have to take over as leaders of the Treasure Hoarders just to get Reed Miller's treasure? Honestly, all this heir talk is weirding Paimon out...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's hard to imagine anyone leading the Treasure Hoarders...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Exactly — there are people who call themselves Treasure Hoarders in every corner of Teyvat these days. And that's where the problem lies.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: While we might be able to face reality, my stubborn old grandmother still dreams of a day when the Treasure Hoarders can restore their glory from the days of Reed Miller.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: She fantasizes that someone will come along and rally the masses — "Let the dead bury the dead, and rise to build an Elysium for the hungry and the poor on the wealth of the high and haughty."

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: While most of us have heard how Reed Miller stole from the rich to help the poor, very few know that the Treasure Hoarders once defended Elysium from the dark abyss...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: It was the Treasure Hoarders' golden age — it was the worst of times, and yet somehow it was also the best.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: I don't know, maybe things are still the same today. But that era has passed, and she'll have to accept that someday.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're not wrong... but what are we supposed to do about it?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #Before we go any further, {NICKNAME}, are you willing to serve as heir to the Treasure Hoarders and see that Reed Miller's dream is one day fulfilled?

choices.text: I have my own dreams to fulfill...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Haha, just as I thought. Then how about we do it this way... Let's put on a little show!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Again!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's what you said back at Blue Amber Lake. Sure, you helped us get the Proof of the Cognoscenti back then... but who knows when you'll use those same sneaky tricks on us!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Why would I do anything to thwart you when we're already such good friends? Now, instead of being suspicious, how about we focus on what we're going to say.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You have a brief discussion with Tolfin about how to convince Hiljetta...\nAccording to Tolfin, simply mentioning the name "Avrelian" should be enough to gain her trust, and if she ever brings up the name "Brahe," all you have to say is that you don't agree with his methods.\nAs for who these two people actually are, Tolfin says it's a long story and promises to explain everything in detail when he gets the chance...

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: #So, what do you say, little {M#lad}{F#lass}? Are you in?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I will fulfill Avrelian's dream.

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: Good! That's the spirit. If it weren't for the little brat acting just like that good-for-nothing Brahe, the Proof of the Cognoscenti wouldn't have been scattered and lost for so long.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're nothing like Tolfin... or that Brahe-ma-call-it fellow! You can rest assured!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #*sigh* Even I have to admit that {NICKNAME} is the most suitable candidate to inherit the Great Treasure.

response.speaker: Hiljetta
response.text: Then it's settled, all that's left is for you to retrieve the Great Treasure. At the treasure site, you'll likely run into a few tricks left behind by that good-for-nothing... Hmph! I'm sure you'll be able to handle anything he came up with.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Paimon still has no idea where "East of the Moon, West of the Sun" could be...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Oh, that... Well, it's beyond the horizon, yet so close you can touch it. Also, I won't be joining you for the next trial, so here's wishing you all the best!

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Still, I'll be in Piramida for a little while longer, so please let me know if everything goes well. I'm counting on the both of you.

choices.text: I just want to inherit the treasure he left behind...
I swear I had no idea...

talks.objective: Go "East of the Moon, West of the Sun"

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Ha! So this is what "Bounty Island" looks like. I guess it really does live up to its name.

dialogues.speaker: Silve
dialogues.text: What are we going to do with the loot? Same as usual? Though, if we're taking it back to Snezhnograd...

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Why not give it to the kids on the streets? I ran into them a few days ago while out on patrol. That kid with the conch shell struck me as a smart one.

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: They'll know what to do with the treasure — and who best to share it with.

dialogues.speaker: Silve
dialogues.text: Suits me, let's do it your way.

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: But compared to the treasures on display in the governor's palace, these little trinkets are hardly even worth the bother...

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Hmph... Even in a backwater like this, those arrogant fools still indulge in their outrageous extravagance... Their shiny facade can't hide the fact they're already rotten to the core.

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Have you seen it yet? This place is no different from Snezhnograd.

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Are we really supposed to fight to protect people like this? And protect them from those we have no quarrel with? The unseen, the downtrodden, the despised...

dialogues.speaker: Silve
dialogues.text: I understand your anger. But there's not much we can do.

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: There's not much we can do right now. But sooner or later, we have to upturn the status quo, to weed out the corruption root and stem. I must rise to the top — by any means necessary...

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: I count myself lucky to have ended up fighting by your side, Silve. But I often find myself looking back to where I came from...

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: It's a place my brothers and sisters remain — where they continue to endure hardships they should never have to bear. Tell me, those innocent souls — were they born to suffer like this?

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: If it's the law that is causing their suffering, then I shall rewrite the law. And if it's the corrupt nobles, then I shall purge them from their ranks!

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: One day, I'll raise an Elysium that belongs to us on this land — a land that has always belonged to us!

dialogues.speaker: Silve
dialogues.text: I believe in you, Relya. I know you can accomplish your dream.

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: ...Let's not talk about that now. Even thieves have their code, so I'll leave this behind. That way, the governor will know who took his treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Silve
dialogues.text: It's just a pity I won't get to see his reaction myself.

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Haha, that would be a sight to behold.

talks.objective: Enter the treasure site
Find a way to open the door and leave

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: #What's the matter, {NICKNAME}? Something else on your mind?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: The name "Reed Miller" was merely an alias, a mask to hide one's true identity. To the poor, Miller was a figure of admiration, while to the nobles, the very mention of him would draw curses and swearing. But it was never the name of just one person.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Even among the earliest Treasure Hoarders, there were already three individuals who went by the name "Reed Miller." And that doesn't even include those who later chose to pose as Miller for one reason or another.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Why, just last week, I had a run-in with two petty thieves, both calling themselves Miller, who attempted to steal my harp. But that's a story for another time.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: #Putting the latter-day pretenders aside, I do know a thing or two about the original trio. So, {NICKNAME}, which of the three are you asking about?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: The first to use this alias was <color=#00E1FFFF>Avrelian</color>. I've mentioned him to you two before.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He was an orphan who was adopted by a rank-and-file military officer named Mikhnenko after losing both his parents. As a result, he was able to attend the Snezhnayan Royal Military Academy.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Interestingly, according to official records, shortly after Avrelian became a non-commissioned officer, he "died in the line of duty" for unknown reasons. Perhaps this was his way of getting out of the military — although I can't say for sure.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Whatever the reason, he surfaced in Nod-Krai a few years later under the name Reed Miller, gathering the destitute who lived on the fringes of society into a band that became the first Treasure Hoarders.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: At that time, they recognized this young man from who-knows-where as their leader, believing that he would free them from their shackles and build an Elysium where all would stand equal.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Unfortunately, even I cannot say what his true motive was, nor can I tell you much about how the Treasure Hoarders operated at this time.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Maybe he had a grand dream; maybe, like my grandmother, he possessed a strong, unshakable faith... or maybe he harbored some other darker, more personal motive he couldn't share with anyone... Alright, please don't tell my grandmother I said that last part.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Anyhow, all of that happened five centuries ago. For most people, the only thing known about the very first Treasure Hoarder is what eventually became of him, which was death by execution in Snezhnograd.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Although he had never been captured by the authorities before, he was convinced by a noble friend to walk away from his organization, leave everything behind, and go to Snezhnograd — supposedly to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar or something like that.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Unsurprisingly, he was promptly sent to his death without so much as a glimpse of the Tsar.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: That's why I say, thieves and nobles don't belong together. It only ever ends in tragedy.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: The second "Reed Miller" was a woman whose real name I do not know. All I know is that she was a traitor to the Frostmoon Scions, who struck her name from history altogether.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: In truth, I have no idea what her connection to Avrelian was. And as for the Frostmoon Scions of five hundred years ago... Well, it was a pretty creepy place to be, judging from the poems I've read.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: According to Brahe, the entirety of Hiisi Island was encircled by a golden wall even taller than Mont Esus in Fontaine. So I really have no good explanation for how she could have come to know Avrelian.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: And now, the Frostmoon Scions have transformed into something entirely different, so much so that I even wonder if they're too gullible these days.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: That's why I told Miss Hidimbi just a few days ago that she was real, real lucky. Had she tried to dupe the Frostmoon Scions of five hundred years ago, she'd probably be with Al-Ahmar by now.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: So anyway, after Avrelian was executed, she began donning that silver mask, claiming to be the "master thief Reed Miller who had escaped the gallows."

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: She molded the Treasure Hoarders into a highly disciplined, quasi-military force that almost resembled a religious order. Her mantra was that no one should place their faith in gods or deities, for it was humanity alone that held the power to save its own.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Strange as it may sound, the best way to describe the Treasure Hoarders of that era might simply be "an irreligious religious order."

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Under the name "Reed Miller," she gathered a large group of bandits, and together, they picked the governor's palace in Nod-Krai clean in a single night.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: All the countless curios, antiques, Mora, and jewels that they made off with... She gave all of that away to the poor of Nasha Town. This was the very "storm of gold and silver" that the cheap novels so fancifully describe.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: And now, in Nod-Krai, the people absolutely revere Miller... But if you ask me, that has nothing to do with Avrelian's dream, the dream that my grandmother believes in so staunchly.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: For most of the people living on this land, both his dream and Elysium are as distant as the moon.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Who knows, maybe they're just dreaming of someone like her — someone who'd drop loot from nowhere right into their laps, without them having to lift a finger.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: It's a bit embarrassing for me to say this, but of the three "Reed Millers," the one I mentioned earlier, <color=#00E1FFFF>Brahe</color>, is the one my grandmother really despises.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Much as my grandmother doesn't want to admit it, he is actually our forebear.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He was of a station even higher than Solovei the Torchforger — he was the adoptive son of the fae lord Trubetskoy, governor of all Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Some have claimed he was actually the governor's illegitimate son. And because the blood of the fae ran through his veins, he was more handsome than most people you'd ever meet.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Of course, that's probably just an unfounded rumor. I mean, surely neither of you can find any trace of fae blood in my face, can you?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Like Avrelian, he was a student at the military academy, though he enrolled long after Avrelian had graduated. I doubt the two of them ever crossed paths there.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: After graduating from the academy, Brahe returned to Nod-Krai, where, like every other Snezhnayan noble of the time, he settled into a life of indulgence and decadence.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: That is, until the night he caught a glimpse of the second "Reed Miller" as she looted the governor's palace.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Brahe fell in love with the Frostmoon Scion turncoat at first sight. So enamored was he that he even abandoned his life as a noble to join the Treasure Hoarders.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: "The nobility are at leisure to see the suffering of others as a beautiful, romantic fantasy, whereas the truly destitute are relegated to soulless villainy and rogues' roles in every tale..."

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: This is why my grandmother despises him so much. In her view, he was the one who tainted Avrelian's dream, the one who turned a name that rightfully belonged to the poor into one from a farcical story of romance.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: But it's just that... He abandoned his life as a noble after his beloved passed and continued to rob the rich to help the poor and aid the people of this land...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: So no matter what his motives were, or how he went about achieving his goals, I don't think it can be said he tainted Avrelian's name. Not when we consider how many people he helped and how much he bettered their lives.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: It's no exaggeration to say that of all the stories about the master thief Reed Miller that can be found in the cheap novels out there...

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Maybe one in five is about the traitorous Frostmoon Scion. Three in ten tell Brahe's tale, and the remaining half is just pure fiction, fabricated solely to tantalize and reel in the reader.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: While my grandmother may be a steadfast believer in Reed Miller's dream, just what exactly is this dream? Even Brahe might not have fully understood it back in the day, so how could we claim to now?

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Having said that... maybe all that doesn't really matter after all, as long as you believe in something. One must believe in something, if only to be able to have the courage to face the morrow.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Yes, I'll see you around. May your journey ahead be smooth and beautiful, just like this tune.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Iron Coins were a form of currency issued by Avrelian... that is, the very first "Reed Miller."

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He believed that in a world without divisions, in an Elysium where no one went hungry or suffered from the cold, people should not be relying on wealth bestowed and governed by the gods to help each other.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: He believed that people should be the masters of wealth, not its slaves. And even if mastering the "heart of gold" might be an impossible task, everyone should have the right to wield the wealth that belongs to all to begin with.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: But as you both can see, the Iron Coins he imbued with meaning quickly became worthless scrap metal after his death, largely due to the very "people" he had placed his faith in.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Oh, and by the way, there's another piece of info that came to me on the wind, though I cannot guarantee its veracity. And since I have no way to verify it, please take it as you will.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: In Snezhnaya, there's a Fatui Harbinger with a rather peculiar obsession. He seeks to create a more perfect economic order in this world.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Unfortunately, he is not a collector of Iron Coins. Otherwise, you might be able to make a whole fortune in Mora by selling these to him.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: It was the third "Reed Miller," that is, the one named Brahe, who left behind the legend of the "Great Treasure."

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: As for why he did that... Maybe he just wanted to keep future generations of treasure hunters hooked, so that the name "Reed Miller" would never be forgotten.

response.speaker: Tolfin
response.text: Yes, I'll see you around. May your journey ahead be smooth and beautiful, just like this tune.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Huh!? Wha!?! What just happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We found a Treasure Hoarder ship under a pile of Iron Coins, then you took the helm... After that, it felt like a dream, and then somehow, we ended up here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those two... they mentioned someone called "Brahe." Either it's a crazy coincidence, or they must be from a long, long time ago?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: At the very least, we know they have a connection to this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! And from what they were saying, there was once some treasure buried here, and even though they made off with it, it seems they left something else in its place...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been so long, who knows if someone's already dug it up by now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's see if we can find it first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, it can't hurt to look! If Paimon remembers correctly, it should be somewhere around... here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe it's still here! Why didn't the governor come to collect it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This is what they left here? Isn't this...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon doesn't understand. Let's ask Tolfin about it... Oh! Paimon almost forgot, we should tell him what happened with the Great Treasure, too!

dialogues.text: Bounty Island's just up ahead. Nothing about it looks particularly special from here.
Relya, I'm still not happy about this. I mean, the treasure here's been marked by the governor. If we take it...

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Don't worry. We still have a few more days before the drill's over, and by the time the governor notices, we'll already be in Snezhnograd. No one'll think to come after us.
That's not what's bothering me... What if he ends up on the hook for telling us where the treasure is?

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: ...Who? Oh, you mean that Brahe kid. What do you care? He's had his fair share of "the honey brewed for the few."
And I haven't?

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? You and that kid are nothing alike. If you were on the same side as them, you wouldn't...

dialogues.speaker: Relya
dialogues.text: Ah! Don't worry about him, he'll be fine. He might be adopted, but he's still the governor's son. Besides, he's young — no one's gonna give him any trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Silve
dialogues.text: I hope you're right.

talks.objective: Talk to Tolfin

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: #Oh, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Have you two found the Great Treasure already?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If you mean that pile of old Iron Coins...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We left those Iron Coins exactly where we found them... Well, actually, they're on top now.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Tolfin what happened at the treasure site and the strange things that happened after you boarded the ship...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For some reason, they left behind some sort of raven insignia.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: It seems the earth remembers far more than we could ever imagine — as a storyteller, I can't help but feel humbled by that...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: After all, human life is fleeting, and oral history is prone to errors — some stories may even be lost forever. Yet the earth's memory no doubt remains true.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: I think it could only have been Avrelian who left that "raven insignia." You may be more familiar with another of his names — Reed Miller.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? You mean that was the legendary thief, Reed Miller? Paimon would never have guessed by looking at him...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: From what you described, the things you saw almost certainly happened before the Treasure Hoarders were even formed. It's said that back then, he liked to play the role of heroic thief with his military academy buddies, stealing from the rich and helping the poor.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: In fact, that raven insignia was derived from the family crest of his noble-born academy classmate.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: But that's all in the past, so I shalln't bore you with the details. Anyway, seeing as our fates appear to be intertwined, how about you two take this raven insignia as a keepsake?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I assume accepting this doesn't automatically make me the Treasure Hoarders' heir...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Haha, there's no need to worry — like I said, the golden age of the Treasure Hoarders is over. However, there is still one slight problem...

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: My stubborn grandmother seems to have taken a liking to you. If she ever asks you for a friendly sparring match, please don't turn her down — and don't pull your punches, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, she's so much stronger than a regular old lady, we wouldn't dream of doing anything but pummeling her with everything we've got!

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Well then, the Great Treasure buried "East of the Moon, West of the Sun" has been claimed by a pair of remarkable adventurers, and this performance, too, has come to its close.

dialogues.speaker: Tolfin
dialogues.text: Allow me to play you a tune, to express my wish that every step of your journey be filled with mystery, and every path may bring you jubilation.
